method.method_draft: Read from the image that all six marked points lie on grid intersections, and in particular there are two adjacent marked points on the left vertical grid line at (0,3) and (0,4), plus the top marked point at (1,0). From the text, we need the smallest possible area among triangles using three marked points. Use the lattice-area fact: any triangle whose vertices are lattice points has area an integer multiple of 1/2, so no nonzero triangle can have area smaller than 1/2. Then exhibit a triangle of area 1/2: take the adjacent left points as a vertical base of length 1, and the point (1,0), whose perpendicular distance to that vertical line is 1. Its area is (1/2)(1)(1)=1/2. Therefore the minimum is 1/2.
